transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I came in because I just can’t sit still. It feels like I got a motor running inside me all day. Like even sitting here, I’m already wanting to stand up or move around.

It happens at church, or waiting at the clinic, even at home. If I gotta sit still too long, I start feeling trapped, like I need to get up and do something. My aunt used to say I was like that as a kid too—couldn’t stay in one place—but, yeah, that’s why I’m here.
Did this restlessness start after you began taking any psychiatric medicine?

Uh… psychiatric medicine? I don’t know, I don’t really think it started after anything like that. I mean, I’m trying to remember, because sometimes they give you pills and the names all sound the same, you know? My cousin had this whole bag of bottles once and—sorry.

For me, I can’t say I noticed it starting because of medicine. It’s more like it’s just been there, but I’m not totally sure what you mean by psychiatric medicine.
As a child, did teachers or adults often tell you that you had trouble staying seated?

Yeah, yeah, they did. Back when I was a boy in school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I couldn’t stay put. I’d be up out of the chair before class was even done, or talking when I wasn’t supposed to.

I remember one teacher put me right up front, then in the back, then by myself near the door—like that was gonna fix it. And I’d still jump up, get in trouble, you know. My mom would get those notes sent home, and then she’d be mad, and I’d be mad too because I didn’t even feel like I meant to do it half the time.
When you were a kid, did you often have trouble paying attention or finishing schoolwork?

Yeah… I mean, schoolwork, I think so. I’d start listening, like I really would, but then my head would just kinda drift. Same thing still happens now—like if somebody’s telling me ride times, or what to get from the pantry, or plans for church, I catch the first part and then I miss pieces I actually needed.

Back then with school, it was like that too, I guess. The teacher would be talking and I’d be there, but not really getting all of it. Then I’d look down and not know what I was supposed to finish. And then—well, the pantry thing happened last week too, I forgot half the list, but yeah… paying attention was hard.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Um… unusually energized? I don’t know. I mean, I have times where I’m up late, but it’s usually because I’m messing around with something or I can’t settle down, not like I suddenly don’t need sleep.

Like, I’ll stay up watching videos or pacing around, and then the next day I’m tired and cranky. My neighbor used to be out all night fixing cars, and he’d say he only needed two hours, but that’s not really me. I don’t think I’ve had a time where I was just full of energy and barely sleeping like that.
When you feel like you can’t sit still, is it usually because you feel worried or nervous?

Not really nervous, no… I mean, I can get annoyed about it, but it’s more like I got a motor running inside me all day. Like if I’m sitting in church, or waiting here at the clinic, even at home on the couch, I start feeling trapped.

It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking, “Oh no, something bad’s gonna happen.” It’s more my body just keeps saying, get up, move, do something. Like my legs wanna go before I even decide. And then people look at me like I’m being rude, especially at church, but I’m just trying not to crawl out of my skin.

The patient confirms longstanding hyperactivity/restlessness, inability to remain seated, distractibility, and difficulty finishing/listening to instructions across settings.
